title: Anduril lifts valuation to 122 trillion won with employee tender offer
key_facts: Bloomberg News reported on 14 Oct that Anduril is expected to lift its valuation to about $90 billion through a tender offer.
A tender offer lets employees sell their shares to outside buyers; the price is $94.80 per share and the total is capped at $1.3 billion.
Employees in 16 countries can take part; the subscription period runs from 13 Oct to 9 Nov.
In May Anduril raised $5 billion led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz at a $61 billion valuation.
Anduril is co-founded by Palmer Luckey, founder of Oculus VR, and former Palantir employees; it makes autonomous defense systems and military drones.
It was named in the $185 billion Golden Dome missile defense system and won a US Army contract worth up to $20 billion; last year's revenue was $2.2 billion.
